sections.name: Free Datasets & Data Hubs

sections.name: Prompt Libraries & Galleries

sections.whyWorthIt: Prompt quality is the cheapest performance upgrade; a bookmarked library beats re-deriving prompts from memory

sections.entriesLookLike: Model Context Protocol servers with transport, auth, and install command
sections.whyWorthIt: MCP is the de facto plug for coding agents in 2026; the ecosystem has 9,800+ servers and rotates fast — curation is the value

sections.name: Free Hosting & Deploy Tiers
sections.entriesLookLike: Zero-cost deploy targets with sleep policy, bandwidth, and card requirements
sections.whyWorthIt: Free hosting is the most volatile category in the whole app (Heroku 2022, Fly.io Oct 2024, Koyeb card wall Feb 2026, HF Spaces Jul 2026); users need a living matrix

sections.name: Student / OSS / Startup Credit Programs
sections.entriesLookLike: Verified-status programs granting credits across many services
sections.whyWorthIt: One verification unlocks thousands of dollars of compute; the eligibility rules are the hard part, so structured fields matter

sections.name: Free AI Courses & Learning Paths
sections.entriesLookLike: Verified-actually-free courses with level, length, and certificate policy

examples.name: Karpathy Neural Networks: Zero to Hero

sections.whyWorthIt: "Free course" lists are notoriously stale (Google AI Essentials is no longer free as of July 2026) — verified-free tracking is exactly the app's core competency

sections.name: Free Voice / TTS Models
sections.entriesLookLike: Open-weight TTS models/repos with license, language support, and speed
sections.whyWorthIt: Voice is the most under-covered modality in the app; free TTS quality crossed the usable line in 2025-26 and pairs with local runtimes

sections.name: System Prompts & Agent Rules Collections
sections.entriesLookLike: Repos/directories of CLAUDE.md, cursor rules, copilot instructions, slash commands
sections.whyWorthIt: The Configs exporter already exists — rules/prompt packs are the raw material users feed it; collection quality varies wildly so curation helps

sections.name: Benchmark Leaderboards
sections.entriesLookLike: Live leaderboards with methodology notes and update cadence
sections.whyWorthIt: Free-model rotation strategy needs an objective "which free model is actually best this month" signal — the app's rate-limit matrix is incomplete without quality data

sections.name: Free AI Newsletters & Official Changelogs
sections.entriesLookLike: Curated newsletters plus first-party changelog pages, with frequency
sections.whyWorthIt: Free tiers change monthly (see recentFreeTierChanges); changelogs are the earliest warning signal and directly feed the app's staleness detection

sections.name: AI Browser Extensions
sections.entriesLookLike: Browser add-ons for chat/sidebar/automation, with local-model support flags
sections.whyWorthIt: Extensions are how non-terminal users touch AI; local-runtime-compatible ones (Page Assist ↔ Ollama) bridge perfectly to the app's Runtimes section

sections.name: Hugging Face Spaces Worth Bookmarking
sections.entriesLookLike: Notable public Spaces (demos/arenas/tools) with task and hardware tier
sections.whyWorthIt: Free hosted AI demos are the fastest zero-install way to test a capability before committing local VRAM — but the free-tier rules changed July 2026 (Gradio/Docker Spaces now PRO-gated), so labeling which run free matters

sections.name: Free CI
sections.entriesLookLike: CI services with free minutes, runner OS support, and private-repo rules
sections.whyWorthIt: AI-adjacent devs burn CI on eval pipelines and model packaging; free-minute policies differ sharply for private repos and macOS runners

sections.name: Free Auth / DB / Storage Tiers
sections.entriesLookLike: Backend building blocks with free-row/GB limits and pause policies
sections.whyWorthIt: Every AI side project needs auth+DB+storage; pause/expiration policies on free tiers (Render Postgres dies in 30 days) are exactly the gotcha fields the app tracks well

offlineData.answer: For first-launch/offline value, ship a bundled, timestamped snapshot: (1) the full bookmarks DB (all categories, with descriptions, favicon hashes, and lastVerified dates) as a local SQLite/JSON file; (2) the rate-limit matrix as cached JSON with per-entry lastVerified timestamps and a staleness badge computed on launch; (3) a bundled model catalog for the Runtimes section — model name, parameter count, GGUF file size, quantized VRAM/RAM requirement, and which local daemon (Ollama/LM Studio/Jan) serves it; (4) preloaded system-prompt/rule packs (CLAUDE.md templates, cursor rules, copilot instructions) as static assets for the Configs exporter; (5) the recentFreeTierChanges log as an offline changelog so users see what changed even without network; (6) a local fuzzy-search index (e.g., FTS5) over all of the above so the app is fully usable offline; (7) default export templates for the top IDEs/agents; (8) locally cached favicons and a fallback letter-icon set; (9) encrypted Key Vault schema ready for keys, with the verification checklist stored locally so verification steps are visible offline; (10) an onboard 'starter pack' of the 25 highest-value bookmarks per persona (ML tinkerer, web dev, agent builder) so first launch isn't empty.
